assessment.rationale: The customer uses express.json() and computes the HMAC over JSON.stringify(req.body), which re-serializes the parsed body instead of using the raw bytes. This is the first cause listed in KB-013, so it is a configuration issue and not a Meridian defect.

traces.reply: Hi Wrenfield Payroll, thanks for the details and the logs. The cause is most likely in your handler rather than the signature itself. Your code runs express.json() and then hashes JSON.stringify(req.body). Re-serializing the parsed JSON changes spacing and key order, so the HMAC will not match. Meridian computes the signature over the raw request body, so you need to verify against the raw bytes. In Express, use a raw body parser (for example express.raw) on the webhook route, compute the HMAC-SHA256 on those bytes, and compare with a constant-time check. Then use Send test event in Settings > Webhooks to confirm. The full steps are in [KB-013], and the verification process is in [KB-011]. If it still fails after that, a support engineer will follow up.

traces.reply: Hi Kettleby Foods, sorry for the frustration. Here is how to rotate the key. Go to Settings > API keys and click Rotate next to the key. Meridian creates a new key with the same scopes. The old key keeps working for 24 hours, so you can deploy the new key without breaking production. After that it stops working and returns 401 Unauthorized. Since a contractor had access, you can also revoke the old key instead. Revoking stops it right away, so only do that once the new key is deployed. Store the new key in a secrets manager or environment variable. Full steps are in [KB-006]. If anything in the dashboard does not match this, a support engineer will follow up.
